category_title: Preschoolers with aggressive behaviors and social-emotional regulation challenges
minimal_context: Joshua is participating in free play activities and is expected to share toy trucks with a classmate.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Joshua, it is time for free play. You and your classmate can play with the toy trucks together.

STUDENT: I am the boss of the trucks. You have to be the bad guy and I get the big truck.

TUTOR: Let's try to share the toys and play nicely.

STUDENT: (Growls at his classmate) No! We have to play my way!

TUTOR: Joshua, please use your words. What do you think is a good way to play together?

STUDENT: (Yells and throws a toy truck) Do this or I will hurt you!

options.A: Utilize augmenting tactics, such as response promotion and disruption, and reallocate Joshua's responding to options associated with contingent reinforcement during daily free play.
options.B: Read social stories ('It is Hard to Share', 'I Get Angry Sometimes') to the whole group every day before free play, ensuring Joshua and others have time to process them.
options.C: Place an exclusive display board in the classroom solely for Joshua to display his preferred toy trucks and materials during daily free play.
options.D: Implement simultaneous stimulation of nonverbal communication from the perspective of total communication during daily free play activities to address Joshua's peer interactions.
